original_question: If you had a printed version of the whole of (say, the English) Wikipedia, how many printers would you need in order to keep up with the changes made to the live version?
short_answer_summary: About six constantly running inkjet printers at source-era edit rates, with enormous ink expense and paper accumulation.
detailed_scientific_explanation: Rather than estimating words changed, assume each edit entails replacing one page; multipage changes and reverts roughly balance. At90–100 edits/minute and15 pages/minute per printer, about six printers keep pace.
Using Rob Matthews’s featured-article book and average lengths, the author estimates the full English Wikipedia printout at300m³. Keeping up with edits generates this same paper volume every month.

Electricity, printers and staffing are smaller costs than consumables. Paper costs roughly$1,000/day; ink at5–30cents/page yields four or five figures/day, approaching half a million dollars in a month or two. Laser printing is preferable; the chapter ultimately recommends digital.

footnotes.detail: Footnote notes mind-bending filing system needed.

uncertainties_and_limitations: 2014-era site size, rates and printer prices; not current.
extraction_notes: Source transcript is machine OCR and requires line-by-line proofreading against page images.
